summary: Gone Kiona Peak lookout site in Lewis County, WA: D-6 cupola built 1917, L-4 cab 1935, abandoned 1963 for a Watch Mountain tower; cables and old boards remain.

facts.design: D-6 cupola (1917), replaced by an L-4 cab (1935)
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1963 when a new tower went up on Watch Mountain. Willhite describes cables and old boards still on the cliff.

staffing.status: used by the AWS from 1942 to 1944; no later staffing in the sources

access.note: Willhite says the most direct routes have gates and no-trespassing signs, and describes a logging-road approach of more than 10 miles one way that he did not take. Firetower.org lists the Department of Natural Resources as administrator.

visit.trail_note: Willhite calls the approach long and difficult, and says the logging-road route he recommends is over 10 miles one way.

corrections.proposed: D-6 cupola (1917), replaced by an L-4 cab (1935)
corrections.why: The first lookout here was a D-6 cupola built in 1917. The L-4 cab came in 1935, so L-4 alone leaves out the original design.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com's heading reads R.I.P. 1917-1935, but its text, Firetower.org and Willhite all date the end of the site to 1963. The 1935 date is the cab replacement.
Firelookout.com places the new tower 3 miles east of the site; Willhite says West Watch Mountain. The story says only Watch Mountain.

notes_for_editor: History is consistent across three sources. What remains today and the access picture rest on Willhite alone; his photo captions are labelled 2015 and his page describes the summit without a visit date. The approach crosses gates and no-trespassing signs, so the story does not suggest a route. Corrections: the record's design L-4 omits the 1917 D-6 cupola.
